subject: Temporary SLA circuit-breaker + on-call coverage request — FastCommerce migration
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@fastcommerce.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+contracts@fastcommerce.com
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary SLA exception: weekend P2 response during migration

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from the FastCommerce ops team — we have a cross-region database migration scheduled for the weekend of Sep 20-24. The migration will throttle background writes and will likely trigger a spike in support tickets (mainly P2s) as customers run synchronization jobs.

Given the expected volume and reduced on-call headcount on weekends, we would like to request a temporary SLA exception for P2 response on weekends only (extend response window from 2 hours to 6 hours) for the migration window. We also want to request assistance from Redwood for two items:

- A short-term on-call augmentation: one additional responder for two weekend shifts (Sep 21 and Sep 22, 10:00–18:00 PT).
- A "circuit-breaker" policy that throttles non-critical API jobs and returns a readable maintenance notice when backend latency exceeds the configured threshold. That fallback should reduce alert noise and prevent cascading P1s.

Attached is our maintenance window summary (FC-maintenance-window.pdf) and an initial mutual action plan (FC-MAP-v2.xlsx). We are open to tradeoffs — e.g., a small service credit if we need extended P2 windows, or a documented acceptance test for the circuit-breaker behavior.

Please let me know what Redwood needs from our side to proceed (PO, signed MAP, timesheet for the extra on-call). We have legal and procurement on standby.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Head of Platform Operations, FastCommerce
Aisha.Patel@fastcommerce.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA exception: weekend P2 response during migration

Aisha — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Looping in Ben (support lead) and Lauren (account owner) to evaluate on-call capacity and the circuit-breaker options. A few quick questions to help us scope:

1) Can you confirm expected increase in ticket volume (baseline vs projected) and which endpoints/jobs drive most of the noise?
2) For the circuit-breaker: do you want Redwood to implement a tenant-level throttling + maintenance response, or do you prefer we provide the primitives (threshold alerts + toggle) and FastCommerce to flip it?
3) Do we need an audiovisual notification (SMS/phone) for escalations during the window, or email + PagerDuty alerting is sufficient?

If you can sign the MAP and confirm budget for two weekend augmentations, we can stand up the circuit-breaker toggle and schedule Redwood responders. Ben — can you review the technical ask and draft an on-call rota? Lauren — we may need a quick procurement path for a one-off overtime/augmentation addendum.

Thanks — I’ll try to get a proposed plan out today.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Sep 12, 2028 at 8:14 AM Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@fastcommerce.com> wrote:
> Quick note from the FastCommerce ops team — we have a cross-region database migration scheduled for the weekend of Sep 20-24...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 12:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA exception: weekend P2 response during migration

Marissa — thanks for pulling me in. Quick technical notes and proposal:

- Circuit-breaker approach: Redwood can enable a tenant-scoped middleware that responds with HTTP 503 + a structured JSON maintenance payload for non-critical endpoints once tail latency > 3s for 3 consecutive minutes. That will prevent downstream retries from overwhelming the system.
- We can expose a managed toggle in the console with the ability to auto-enable when latency crosses thresholds; we will also add a manual override.
- For P2 handling: recommended model is to extend weekend P2 to 6 hours for the migration window, but maintain P1 targets unchanged. We'll auto-route P1s to priority on-call with SMS escalation.
- On-call augmentation: I propose two paid weekend shifts covered by Redwood senior on-call (Ben + one backup). Cost estimate: two 8-hour shifts weekembar (OT rate) ~ $3,200.
- Acceptance tests: FastCommerce to provide a small set (5) of smoke scenarios we can run in staging and one production verification step post-toggle activation.

Attached: draft MAP with responsibilities and timing (FC-MAP-v2.xlsx). If legal needs a signed DocuSign for the one-off SLA exception/credit, we can route that once terms are agreed.

Ben
Head of Support Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: approval request — FastCommerce weekend SLA exception

Marissa — summarizing for approval:

- Ask: Temporary weekend P2 response window extended to 6 hours for Sep 20-24 (weekend shifts Sep 21–22).
- Mitigations: Tenant-level circuit-breaker, manual toggle, auto-P1 escalation to SMS on-call.
- Cost: Estimated $3,200 (OT + senior on-call premium).
- Conditions for approval: Signed MAP, FastCommerce to provide 5 acceptance tests, Redwood to run one production verification after toggle.
- Proposed escalation path during the window:
  1) P2s triaged by Redwood weekend responder (Ben or assigned backup).
  2) If incident classified P1, immediate SMS to senior on-call, then 15-min bridge setup.
  3) If circuit-breaker triggers repeatedly (>3 events in 1 hour), open an immediate SEV bridge and escalate to leadership.

I recommend we approve on the conditions above and offer a one-time 5% service credit if the turnaround exceeds the temporary P2 window more than twice during the migration.

Approve?

Soojin
Support Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@fastcommerce.com>, ops+contracts@fastcommerce.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLA exception: weekend P2 response during migration — APPROVED (conditions)

Aisha — thanks for your patience. Redwood approves the temporary weekend SLA exception for FastCommerce with the following conditions (effective Sep 20 00:00 PT through Sep 24 23:59 PT):

1) P2 weekend response window extended to 6 hours for the dates above. P1 targets unchanged.
2) Redwood will enable a tenant-scoped circuit-breaker as described by Ben. Default trigger: tail latency > 3s for 3 consecutive minutes. We will add a manual override toggle in the console.
3) Redwood will provide two senior weekend shifts (Ben + named backup) on Sep 21 and Sep 22, 10:00–18:00 PT. Cost: estimated $3,200; Redwood will invoice FastCommerce after the window.
4) Conditions: FastCommerce signs the updated MAP (DocuSign link below) and provides the 5 acceptance tests at least 48 hours before Sep 20. Redwood to run a single production verification step post-toggle activation.
5) Credits: If more than two P2 responses exceed the temporary window during the migration, Redwood will apply a one-time 5% service credit to the following invoice.

Escalation path during the window: P2 handling by weekend responder → P1 immediate SMS escalation → 15-min bridge → Leadership notification if unresolved beyond 60 minutes or repeated circuit-breaker triggers.

DocuSign (sign MAP): https://www.docusign.com/track/ABCDEF-123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FC-2028-0921
Internal runbook: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/123456/runbook-circuit-breaker

Please sign the MAP and confirm acceptance tests. Once signed, we'll enable the toggle in staging and schedule the verification run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
